For every $m\in\mathbb N_0$ and real $T$, the extension in [[def-boys-function-and-coulomb-auxiliary-recurrence]] satisfies
$$0<F_m(T)\le\frac1{2m+1},\qquad F_m(0)=\frac1{2m+1},$$
$$F_m(T)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-T)^k}{k!(2m+2k+1)},\qquad \frac{d}{dT}F_m(T)=-F_{m+1}(T).$$
The upper bound in the first display is asserted for $T\ge0$. For $T>0$ the function also satisfies
$$2T F_{m+1}(T)=(2m+1)F_m(T)-e^{-T},\qquad F_m(T)=\frac{\gamma(m+\tfrac12,T)}{2T^{m+1/2}}.$$
The complete Gamma factor at a half-integer is
$$\Gamma(m+\tfrac12)=\frac{(2m)!}{4^m m!}\sqrt\pi.$$

For $x\in\mathbb R$, define
$$\exp(x):=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{x^n}{\iota(n!)}, \qquad e:=\exp(1),$$
provided by the all-real convergence proved in [[lem-exponential-series-has-infinite-radius]]. Here $n!\in\mathbb N$ is the factorial of [[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]], $\iota(n!)$ is its nonzero real image ([[def-canonical-natural]], [[lem-of-naturals-positive]]), and powers and series are those of [[def-integer-power]] and [[def-series]].

This is a real power series centred at $0$ ([[def-real-power-series-and-radius-of-convergence]]). No logarithm, irrational power, or differential equation enters the definition.

Let $m,N\in\mathbb N_0$, $T\ge0$, and $N+2\ge T$. Then
$$\left|F_m(T)-\sum_{k=0}^N\frac{(-T)^k}{k!(2m+2k+1)}\right|\le\frac{T^{N+1}}{(N+1)!(2m+2N+3)}.$$
In particular, this is a valid finite Taylor certificate whenever $0\le T\le1$.

Let $m\ge0$, $T>0$, and let $I_m=[c_m-r_m,c_m+r_m]$ enclose $F_m(T)$ while $J=[c_e-r_e,c_e+r_e]$ encloses $e^{-T}$. The exact upward recurrence image for $F_{m+1}$ has radius at most
$$\frac{(2m+1)r_m+r_e}{2T},$$
and the exact downward recurrence image for $F_m$, from an interval of radius $r_{m+1}$ for $F_{m+1}$, has radius at most
$$\frac{2Tr_{m+1}+r_e}{2m+1}.$$
Outward-rounded intervals add at most the mean of the two endpoint-rounding errors to these radii. Iterating the displayed bounds gives valid finite error-amplification estimates for any requested order range. Upward recurrence is undefined at $T=0$; direct values $F_m(0)=1/(2m+1)$ are exact.

Every call to [[alg-certified-boys-finite-budget-branch-evaluation]] terminates after finitely many operations bounded by its declared caps. Whenever it returns `success` on $\mathcal T\subset[0,\infty)$, each returned interval $I_m$ contains the exact range $\{F_m(T):T\in\mathcal T\}$ for $0\le m\le M$ and has the absolute and any reported relative accuracy required by [[def-certified-evaluation-result-contract]]. It may instead return `inconclusive`, `domain`, or `range`; no success for every finite input or cap is asserted.

Input a nonnegative integer $M$, a finite dyadic interval $\mathcal T=[T_-,T_+]\subset[0,\infty)$, absolute tolerance $\varepsilon_a>0$, optional relative tolerance $\varepsilon_r>0$, a finite integer work cap $W$, a finite integer precision cap $P\ge2$, and a dyadic format with precision $2\le p\le P$, exponent bounds and elementary truncation index $K\ge1$. These are the backend parameters of [[def-certified-evaluation-result-contract]]. The output is a table of real dyadic intervals $I_m$ for $0\le m\le M$, with status `success`, `inconclusive`, `domain`, or `range`.

All arithmetic uses [[def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations]]. Every real elementary call means a typed DAG call to [[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]] at the supplied format and fixed $K$. Embed an exact rational argument by outward rounding; check the domain of the entire rounded argument before calling. Square roots use the outward square-root operation. No machine elementary value is an endpoint certificate. Maintain a shared work counter: charge each arithmetic operation, conversion, comparison, loop update, summand and primitive child operation before executing it. Interrupt a child when the remaining counter reaches zero. A cap exhaustion or unresolved enclosure test gives `inconclusive`; a finite endpoint overflow gives `range`. Invalid original inputs give `domain`; a domain test obscured only by intermediate rounding gives `inconclusive`.

1. Validate the stated input conditions and supported format. Process the distinct endpoints in increasing order; process the distinct seed orders $m\in\{0,M\}$ in increasing order. At an endpoint $\tau=0$, form the exact rationals $1/(2m+1)$ for every $0\le m\le M$ and round them outward to the output format. Use this table without a recurrence. A rational is retained exactly internally, but a non-dyadic rational is not returned as a singleton dyadic interval.

2. For each positive endpoint $\tau$, perform refinements $k=0,1,\ldots,W-1$, subject to the shared work counter. At refinement $k$, try the two seed orders separately using their own $m$ and $s=m+\tfrac12$:

   - If $0<\tau\le1$, evaluate the Taylor polynomial through $N=k$ from [[thm-boys-integral-identities-series-and-incomplete-gamma]], then enlarge by the outward upper bound for $\tau^{N+1}/((N+1)!(2m+2N+3))$ from [[lem-boys-small-taylor-remainder]]. The condition $N+2\ge\tau$ holds throughout this branch.
   - If $1<\tau\le2m+1$, use $N=2^k$ panels of [[lem-boys-positive-midpoint-enclosure]], in increasing node order $j=1,\ldots,N$, and enlarge the positive midpoint sum by $(m+\tau)/(2N)$. Its dyadic nodes are formed exactly before storage; evaluate their exponentials by the finite real elementary call.
   - If $\tau>2m+1$, request the Gamma target from [[alg-certified-gamma-loggamma-evaluation]] on the exact rectangle $[s,s]+i[0,0]$, with child absolute tolerance $\varepsilon_a/2^{k+2}$, no relative request, base format precision $p_0=p$, the same exponent bounds and fixed elementary truncation $K$, child precision cap $P$, and child work cap $w=\lfloor R/4\rfloor$, where $R$ is the remaining parent work at call entry. If $w<1$, stop `inconclusive`. Debit its actual work, including unsuccessful work, to the parent counter. A successful child rectangle has real projection containing the real number $\Gamma(s)$: its reality follows from the positive-real Euler integral, also evaluated by the half-integer identity in [[thm-boys-integral-identities-series-and-incomplete-gamma]]. Use this projection as the real Gamma enclosure. Evaluate $e^{-\tau}$ by the real elementary call, and use [[lem-boys-incomplete-gamma-large-t-tail-bound]] to form the enclosing interval for $F_m(\tau)$. Compute $\tau^s=\tau^m\sqrt\tau$ and $\tau^{s-1}=\tau^s/\tau$ by outward operations; the exact denominator $1-\max(s-1,0)/\tau$ is positive. Replace a negative lower endpoint by zero, retaining the upper endpoint. A child `range` propagates `range`; a child `domain` on this valid positive argument or a child `inconclusive` invalidates that seed attempt and permits the next bounded refinement.

   A finite seed interval is available to its direction only when its radius is at most $\varepsilon_a$. A failed attempt does not invalidate a successfully enclosed seed for the other direction. Every panel and child loop is subject to the counter, even when its formal index bound is very large.

3. At each refinement obtain one finite real interval $J$ for $e^{-\tau}$. From an available order-zero seed form the upward candidate for orders $0,\ldots,M$; from an available order-$M$ seed form the downward candidate for orders $M,\ldots,0$. Use the exact affine recurrence maps in [[lem-boys-upward-downward-recurrence-error-amplification]]: compute each affine image's endpoints by exact rational endpoint arithmetic, then convert those two endpoints outward once. Record their two conversion errors and propagate the lemma's radius bounds, including half their sum at each step. This prescription avoids omitting rounding at intermediate nodes. A table is admissible only if every entry satisfies the propagated bound and the requested absolute and, if requested, zero-excluding relative-radius test. Keep the admissible candidate with smaller maximum radius, ties upward. If neither direction is admissible, continue to the next refinement. Once an endpoint table is chosen, proceed to the next endpoint. No upward division is attempted at zero.

4. With both endpoint tables, form $I_m=\operatorname{hull}(I_m(T_+),I_m(T_-))$ for every requested order, using endpoint minima and maxima. By $F'_m(T)=-F_{m+1}(T)<0$ from [[thm-boys-integral-identities-series-and-incomplete-gamma]], this encloses the full range over $\mathcal T$. Return `success` only after every output radius is at most $\varepsilon_a$ and, when relative tolerance is requested, the interval excludes zero and satisfies the relative-radius test in [[def-certified-evaluation-result-contract]]. Otherwise return `inconclusive`. Exhausting the finite refinement list or shared work counter also returns `inconclusive`. An unrepresentable finite output returns `range`. No branch promises success for every valid box or finite cap.

derivations.claim: The exact identity in [F1] divides a difference of two terms. By [F1] and [F3], $F_0(T)=1-T/3+R_F$ with $|R_F|\le T^2/10$. By [F2], $e^{-T}=1-T+R_e$ with $|R_e|\le T^2$ for $T\le1$: for $k\ge2$, $k!\ge2^{k-1}$, so $\sum_{k\ge2}1/k!\le\sum_{k\ge2}2^{1-k}=1$. Therefore $$\left|(F_0(T)-e^{-T})-\frac{2T}{3}\right|\le\frac{11}{10}T^2,$$ so for $T\le1/4$ the positive difference is at least $T/4$. The two terms being subtracted each tend to one as $T\downarrow0$.

Applying [F4] with $m=0$ gives a factor $1/(2T)$ on both seed radii, which diverges as $T\downarrow0$ for fixed nonzero radii. In contrast, [F3] gives a direct Taylor enclosure with error $T^2/10$. The algorithm [F5] can therefore select the direct small-argument branch and return only a certified interval; the example makes no claim that every requested tolerance succeeds under every finite cap.

Let $n,r\ge1$ be integers, $C\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}$, $D\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}$, $H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, and $G\in\mathbb R^{n\times n\times n\times n}$. Define their transformed tensors by
$$H'_{pq}=\sum_{a,b=1}^n C_{ap}H_{ab}C_{bq},\qquad G'_{pqrs}=\sum_{a,b,c,d=1}^n C_{ap}C_{bq}C_{cr}C_{ds}G_{abcd},$$
for $1\le p,q,r,s\le r$. Define the finite **variational energy functional**
$$E(C;D,H,G)=\sum_{p,q=1}^r D_{pq}H'_{pq}+\frac12\sum_{p,q,r,s=1}^r D_{pq}D_{rs}G'_{pqrs}.$$
Its gradient $\nabla_C E$ is the ordinary Euclidean gradient with respect to the $nr$ real entries of $C$. The basis dimension is $n$, the contracted dimension is $r$, and for any finite matrix or tensor $A$, $\|A\|_F=(\sum |A_{i_1\ldots i_k}|^2)^{1/2}$, with the sum over all its entries. This is a finite algebraic functional; it assumes no Hartree–Fock, self-consistency, or minimizing-state postulate.

For perturbed integral tensors $\widetilde H,\widetilde G$, write $\widetilde E$ for the same functional with those tensors and the same fixed $C,D$. The word “variational” here names the finite coefficient functional only; no claim about a stationary point or physical energy is included.

Let $n,r\ge1$, $C\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}$ with $\|C\|_F\le B$, and $D\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}$ with $\|D\|_F\le M$. Suppose $|\widetilde H_{ab}-H_{ab}|\le\varepsilon_2$ and $|\widetilde G_{abcd}-G_{abcd}|\le\varepsilon_4$ for every entry. With the functional of [[def-finite-gaussian-basis-variational-energy-and-gradient]],
$$|\widetilde E-E|\le MrnB^2\varepsilon_2+\frac12M^2r^2n^2B^4\varepsilon_4,$$
and
$$\|\nabla_C\widetilde E-\nabla_CE\|_F\le2nrBM\varepsilon_2+2n^2r^2B^3M^2\varepsilon_4.$$

derivations.claim: There are $2^4=16$ primitive entries, each perturbed by $\varepsilon$, and each product of four coefficients is $K^4$. Thus $\Delta G'_{1111}=16K^4\varepsilon$ and $\Delta E=\tfrac12\Delta G'_{1111}=8K^4\varepsilon$. The perturbed energy is $\tfrac12\varepsilon(C_1+C_2)^4$, so each gradient component is $2\varepsilon(C_1+C_2)^3=16K^3\varepsilon$; its two-entry Frobenius norm is $16\sqrt2K^3\varepsilon$.

Here $B=\|C\|_F=\sqrt2K$ and $M=\|D\|_F=1$. Substitution into [F2] gives energy bound $\tfrac12(1)^2(1)^2(2)^2(\sqrt2K)^4\varepsilon=8K^4\varepsilon$ and gradient bound $2(2)^2(1)^2(\sqrt2K)^3(1)^2\varepsilon=16\sqrt2K^3\varepsilon$, equal to the errors in step 1.1.

Let $a,b>0$, $A,B\in\mathbb R^3$, $p=a+b$, $\mu=ab/p$, and $P=(aA+bB)/p$. Then for every $x\in\mathbb R^3$,
$$\exp(-a\|x-A\|_2^2)\exp(-b\|x-B\|_2^2)=\exp(-\mu\|A-B\|_2^2)\exp(-p\|x-P\|_2^2).$$
For any multi-indices $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb N_0^3$, the polynomial factor $(x-A)^\alpha(x-B)^\beta$ is a finite polynomial in $x-P$ of total degree at most $|\alpha|+|\beta|$. Moreover, $P=(a/p)A+(b/p)B$ lies on the closed segment from $A$ to $B$.

Let $p>0$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^3$. If any component of $\alpha$ is odd, then
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}x^\alpha e^{-p\|x\|_2^2}\,dx=0.$$
If $\alpha_j=2k_j$ for $j=1,2,3$, then
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}x^\alpha e^{-p\|x\|_2^2}\,dx=\pi^{3/2}\prod_{j=1}^3\frac{(2k_j)!}{4^{k_j}k_j!\,p^{k_j+1/2}}.$$
For every $q\in\mathbb N_0$, differentiation with respect to $p$ is valid and
$$\frac{d^q}{dp^q}\int_{\mathbb R^3}x^\alpha e^{-p\|x\|_2^2}\,dx=(-1)^q\int_{\mathbb R^3}\|x\|_2^{2q}x^\alpha e^{-p\|x\|_2^2}\,dx.$$

derivations.claim: By [F1]–[F2], the unnormalized overlap is $(\pi/(a+b))^{3/2}$ and each norm squared is $(\pi/(2a))^{3/2}$ or $(\pi/(2b))^{3/2}$. Multiplying by the normalization constants gives $S(h_a,h_b)=(2\sqrt{ab}/(a+b))^{3/2}$.

The Gram matrix is $\begin{pmatrix}1&S\\S&1\end{pmatrix}$, whose characteristic polynomial is $(1-\lambda)^2-S^2$, so its eigenvalues are $1\pm S$. At $a=b$, $S=1$ and the lower eigenvalue is zero. For $a\ne b$, $2\sqrt{ab}<a+b$, hence $0<S<1$; continuity of the displayed formula gives $S\to1$ as $b\to a$, and therefore $(1+S)/(1-S)\to\infty$.

For pair densities $f,g$ arising as finite products of Gaussian contractions in [[def-cartesian-gaussian-primitives-and-contractions]], let
$$\mathcal C(f,g)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\overline{f(x)}g(y)}{\|x-y\|_2}\,dy\,dx.$$
Then $\mathcal C$ is a well-defined Hermitian positive-semidefinite sesquilinear form on their finite linear span, and
$$|\mathcal C(f,g)|^2\le\mathcal C(f,f)\mathcal C(g,g).$$
For orbitals $\phi_a,\phi_b,\phi_c,\phi_d$ and pair densities $f_{ab}=\overline{\phi_a}\phi_b$, the integral convention in [[def-cartesian-gaussian-primitives-and-contractions]] gives
$$|G(\phi_a,\phi_b;\phi_c,\phi_d)|\le\sqrt{G(\phi_a,\phi_b;\phi_a,\phi_b)G(\phi_c,\phi_d;\phi_c,\phi_d)},$$
where each diagonal quantity is nonnegative. For the real finite energy functional in [[def-finite-gaussian-basis-variational-energy-and-gradient]], let $C\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}$, $D\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}$, and define the input-basis density coefficients $W_{ab}=\sum_{p,q=1}^r C_{ap}D_{pq}C_{bq}$. Here the $n$ input basis functions may themselves be contractions; a primitive basis is the singleton-contraction special case. Reindexing the finite two-body energy gives $E_2=\tfrac12\sum_{a,b,c,d}W_{ab}W_{cd}G_{ab,cd}$. Thus for any finite set $S$ of input-basis quartets omitted from that contraction,
$$B_S=\frac12\sum_{(a,b,c,d)\in S}|W_{ab}W_{cd}|\sqrt{G_{ab,ab}G_{cd,cd}}$$
is an accumulated upper bound for the absolute omitted energy contribution. This does not assert that a screened integral is zero.

Every invocation of [[alg-finite-gaussian-basis-integral-recurrence-evaluation]] terminates after finitely many operations bounded by its work and child-evaluator caps. If it returns `success`, each integral interval contains the exact integral range over the supplied parameter boxes. For the real energy/gradient branch, the returned energy interval and gradient-error bound contain the corresponding values of the finite functional in [[def-finite-gaussian-basis-variational-energy-and-gradient]]. The reported discarded-energy bound is at least the sum of the absolute Cauchy–Schwarz bounds for all skipped terms. The evaluator may return `inconclusive`, `domain`, or `range`; no universal success or exact-sparsity claim is made.

**Inputs.** A finite list of input basis contractions $\phi_a=\sum_{i=1}^{q_a}d_{ai}g_{ai}$, $1\le a\le n$, from [[def-cartesian-gaussian-primitives-and-contractions]], represented by finite dyadic intervals for real centers and positive exponents and finite dyadic intervals or complex rectangles for coefficients; a finite nuclear list; positive integral and energy tolerances for the requested outputs; an optional positive gradient tolerance, defaulting to the energy tolerance when absent; optional positive screening tolerance; finite positive integer work and precision caps $W,P$; and a dyadic format of precision $2\le p\le P$ with exponent bounds and fixed elementary truncation index $K\ge1$. A primitive request is the singleton-contraction case. An energy/gradient request additionally requires $n,r\ge1$, real basis coefficients, real nuclear data, real matrices $C\in\mathbb R^{n\times r},D\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}$ given by dyadic boxes (exact matrices are singleton boxes), and uniform finite bounds $B\ge\sup\|C\|_F$, $M_D\ge\sup\|D\|_F$ from [[def-finite-gaussian-basis-variational-energy-and-gradient]]. Internal primitive labels $(a,i)$ are distinct from the input basis labels $a$; $C$ is a subsequent transform of the input basis.

**Outputs.** A status `success`, `inconclusive`, `domain`, or `range`; outward real intervals or complex rectangles for the requested overlap, kinetic, nuclear-attraction and two-electron Coulomb integrals; when requested, an energy interval, a gradient center and a Frobenius gradient-error bound; and a separately accumulated discarded-energy bound. Success encloses every parameter value in the input boxes. No status declares an omitted integral zero.

**Finite calls and accounting.** Use [[def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations]] for arithmetic. Every real elementary call means a typed DAG call to [[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]] at the supplied format and $K$. Enclose $\pi$ by the $K$-term Machin/arctangent certificate in [[lem-trigonometric-identities-machin-and-range-reduction]], with exact rational tail endpoints before final outward conversion. A shared counter charges each conversion, comparison, loop update, arithmetic operation, recurrence update and summand, including every primitive operation executed by a child. Check the counter before executing an operation and interrupt any child at exhaustion. A required Boys call receives remaining work $R$ as its finite work cap, precision cap $P$, the same format and $K$, absolute tolerance $\varepsilon_I/2$ where $\varepsilon_I$ is the integral tolerance, and no relative request; its actual work is charged to the parent. A required child non-success propagates its status, except that a rounded intermediate failing a domain certification on valid original data yields `inconclusive`. Overflow yields `range`; cap exhaustion yields `inconclusive`. These choices are conservative and need not permit success under every cap or tolerance.

1. Validate positive exponent lower endpoints, finite input boxes, indices in $\mathbb N_0^3$, supported format and positive tolerances/caps. Invalid original data return `domain`. For energy/gradient verify realness and dimensions and certify the norm bounds by outward Frobenius upper bounds on the complete boxes. If this sufficient norm test cannot certify the supplied bounds, return `inconclusive`; do not claim that an unknown represented matrix violates its bound. Form finite requested primitive-pair and quartet lists lexicographically. Include all shifted overlap pairs required by the kinetic raising/lowering formula; a negative index contributes zero.

2. For each ordered primitive pair with exponents $a,b$, indices $\alpha,\beta$ and centers $A,B$, compute $p=a+b$, $P=(aA+bB)/p$, and $K_{ab}=\exp(-ab\|A-B\|^2/p)$ by outward arithmetic and the real elementary call. Compute the Hermite coefficients by [[thm-cartesian-pair-hermite-expansion-and-coefficient-recurrence]], raising the first primitive in x,y,z order and then the second, storing each intermediate degree table until its successors have been formed. The final table has $\prod_{j=1}^3(\alpha_j+\beta_j+1)$ entries; every intermediate table update is also charged. Compute overlap by the finite shifted polynomial expansion and the moments in [[lem-cartesian-gaussian-moments-and-parameter-derivatives]], and kinetic by [[thm-cartesian-gaussian-raising-lowering-and-kinetic-recurrences]]. Certified square roots and integer powers evaluate all half-integer factors in those moment formulas.

3. To evaluate an attraction primitive pair, put $L=|\alpha|+|\beta|$ and use exponent $\eta=p$ and center difference $P-C_{\rm nuc}$. To evaluate a primitive Coulomb quartet, including any diagonal self quartet, put $L=|\alpha|+|\beta|+|\gamma|+|\delta|$, $\eta=pq/(p+q)$ and center difference $P-Q$, where the second pair has exponent $q$. Form the nonnegative Boys argument interval $\mathcal T=\eta\|P-Q\|^2$, with the evident attraction substitution, using interval squaring and the positive exponent bounds. Request Boys orders $0,\ldots,L$ from [[alg-certified-boys-finite-budget-branch-evaluation]]. If rounding prevents certification of a required positive denominator, return `inconclusive`.
